reference.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology / Emery's Principles of Medical Genetics
clinicalPearls: An X-linked recessive disorder causing congenital bilateral blindness in affected males, typically presenting with leukocoria
Caused by mutations in the NDP gene encoding norrin, which regulates retinal vascular development
The retina is severely dysplastic, often with a retrolental fibrovascular mass (pseudoglioma) resembling a mass lesion
Progressive ocular changes include cataract, retinal detachment and eventual shrinkage of the globe (phthisis bulbi)
About a third of patients develop progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and some have developmental or behavioural difficulties
It is an important differential for leukocoria and must be distinguished from retinoblastoma
Female carriers are usually unaffected but can transmit the condition to sons
reference.pathophysiology: Norrie disease is caused by mutations in the NDP gene, which encodes norrin, a secreted protein that activates a Wnt-signalling pathway essential for normal development of the retinal and inner-ear vasculature. Loss of norrin function disrupts retinal angiogenesis, leading to severe retinal dysplasia, failure of normal retinal vascularisation, and formation of a fibrovascular retrolental mass, with progression to retinal detachment and a blind, shrunken eye. The same signalling defect impairs cochlear vascular development, accounting for the later progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and central nervous system involvement can produce cognitive and behavioural features.
additionalDifferentials: Persistent fetal vasculature (persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous)
Familial exudative vitreoretinopathy, also involving the NDP pathway
Retinopathy of prematurity in a preterm infant
Coats disease with exudative retinal detachment
Congenital cataract or other causes of leukocoria
additionalInvestigations: Examination under anaesthesia with detailed fundoscopy in the infant
Ocular ultrasound to characterise the retrolental mass and detachment and help exclude retinoblastoma
MRI when needed to distinguish from an intraocular tumour
Audiological assessment with monitoring for progressive sensorineural hearing loss
Molecular genetic testing of the NDP gene with carrier testing of relatives
redFlags: Leukocoria in an infant, which must be urgently investigated to exclude retinoblastoma
Rapid progression to retinal detachment threatening any residual vision
New or progressive hearing loss requiring audiological review
Developmental regression or behavioural change suggesting central involvement
reference.prognosis: Visual prognosis is very poor, with most affected males blind from birth or early infancy and little response to surgical intervention; sensorineural hearing loss tends to progress over time, and prognosis for hearing and development varies, so long-term multidisciplinary support is needed.
pitfalls: Mistaking the retrolental mass for retinoblastoma or vice versa and delaying correct management
Assuming an isolated eye disorder and not monitoring for later hearing loss
Overlooking the X-linked inheritance and the need for carrier counselling
Attributing developmental problems to visual impairment alone
references: Emery's Elements of Medical Genetics and Genomics
